page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.large is an entry-tier, memory-weighted shared virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 shared vCPUs derived from a single physical core across two hardware threads, driven by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The server is allocated 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an elevated 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent with 0 GPUs, and there is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage volumes for persistent data. The baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark results reflect the limitations of shared hardware threads and legacy Intel Broadwell architecture. Compute performance ranks in the lower tier, with stress-ng single-core scoring 945.88 and multi-core reaching 1857.99, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 2538.35. Extended instruction support includes AVX, BMI2, and AES, though modern AVX-512 extensions are not supported. Memory benchmarks show uncached large-block throughput at 14.95 GB/sec for reads and 11.46 GB/sec for writes. Application-level metrics record 2.53 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 2.31 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary operational tradeoff of the ecs.e4.large lies in its shared CPU provisioning and low baseline bandwidth, which restricts suitability for sustained computational throughput or network-heavy services. However, the generous 16.0 GB memory capacity offers practical resource density for non-critical tasks that require substantial RAM without demanding dedicated CPU cycles. Appropriate workloads include lightweight caching layers, development and testing environments, internal staging platforms, and background batch jobs with modest computing needs.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.large is a memory-weighted shared instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, the instance provides 1 physical core with 2 shared threads, accompanied by a 40 MB L3 cache. It contains no onboard GPUs and does not bundle local storage, requiring attached network disks for file persistence. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates baseline-tier performance across stress-ng compute tests, PassMark metrics, and large-block memory transfers. Its high memory-to-vCPU ratio provides sufficient addressable RAM for light caching, staging environments, and memory-dependent background tasks, though shared compute resources and a baseline network throughput of 0 Gbps make it unsuited for CPU-intensive, high-concurrency production applications.
